records.directQuote: The Se gene is located on chromosome 19 (same as the H gene).
records.explanation: The Se gene codes for the fucosyltransferase involved in type 1 precursor chains and soluble ABH secretions.

records.directQuote: The two alleles at this locus are Le and le.
records.explanation: Lewis antigen production depends on the Lewis (Le) gene; the Se gene affects secretor status.

records.directQuote: the H gene enzymes adds the sugar L-fucose to Type 2 precursor chains
records.explanation: The H gene produces fucosyltransferase acting on type 2 chains; this question uses the user-approved corrected wording.

records.directQuote: All are secretors of ABH soluble antigens.
records.explanation: Le(a-b+) requires Le and Se genes and corresponds to ABH secretor status.

records.directQuote: Lewis genes produce two antigens, Lea and Leb.
records.explanation: Le is the inherited gene required for Lewis antigen production.

records.directQuote: Most often reacts at room temperature, usually IgM
records.explanation: Lewis antibodies, including anti-Leb, most often react at room temperature.

records.directQuote: Vast majority of anti-Lea is IgM and is not clinically significant.
The M and N antigens are found on glycophorin A (GPA)
records.explanation: Glycophorin A carries the M and N antigens.

records.directQuote: The S, s, and U antigens are found on the smaller glycoprotein called glycophorin B (GPB)
records.explanation: Glycophorin B carries S and s (and U).

records.directQuote: The S, s, and U antigens are found on the smaller glycoprotein called glycophorin B (GPB)
records.explanation: The U antigen is carried by glycophorin B.

records.directQuote: usually occurring as a saline agglutinin in antibody tests performed at room temperature.
records.explanation: Anti-M commonly reacts at room temperature.

records.directQuote: Usually, IgG in nature with optimal reactivity at 37oC, binds complement.
records.explanation: Anti-U is usually IgG and reacts optimally at 37°C.
